short_description: 7 printable circle-time talk games for ages 3–7: every question, comment and idea adds a block to the class tower. Script, cards, trackers, slides, story.
long_description:
Talk Tower is a printable circle-time game kit for ages 3–7 (preschool to grade 2), with PDFs and slides. It has seven talk games built around one class tower. Each time a child asks a question, says something back, adds one more idea or shows they listened, a colorful block goes on the tower. Everyone builds one tower together. There are no winners, no points and no blocks taken away.

A one-page teacher script walks you through your first round, word for word. Six more versions follow. Each has a starting age, a 2-minute no-setup version, and ways to make it easier or harder. Prep is about 20 minutes, once, to print and cut. On a busy day, project the slides and play with no cutting at all.

Inside: 32 tower-block turn cards, 36 prompt and topic cards, name blocks, a whose-turn mat, a weekly turn tracker, a Talking Star and a 'Tower wobble!' reset sign, two family take-home pages and a class certificate.

Spoken words in any language, signing, pointing, picture cards and communication devices all earn a block, and 'pass' is always OK. Every play follows our published safety rules.

You get US Letter and A4 PDFs in full color and ink-saver. There is a 20-slide deck to project and a START HERE page. A bonus 32-page story, More Talk, Less Tap, is ready to read aloud. Choose a single-classroom license or a site license for your whole school or center.

compliance_notes: Rule 1: no health, medical or clinical claims; none of the banned clinical or condition words from BRAND.md rule 1 appear anywhere; the kit says it is general classroom play ideas and not a program, assessment, screening tool or professional advice; the tracker says it is a play game, not a measurement or screening tool. No professional-credential authorship implied. Condition-search rule (BRAND.md): no condition keywords, tags or copy in the kit, slides or listing. Rule 2: no school, district, company, app, device or EdTech product named or shown; no local angle; the story's Room 5, Ms. Poppy and children are fictional. Rule 5: no research citations used. Rule 6: talk tips use plain words only (pause and wait, say what you see, repeat and add one word, follow their lead); no trademarked program names. Rule 4 child safety: adult supervision stated on the safety page and family page; paper pieces are large; real blocks or objects near under-3s must be too big to fit through a toilet-paper tube (about 1.25 in / 3.2 cm); Mystery Bag objects follow the same rule; soft large ball rolled on the floor; no balloons under 8; pushpins, staples and small magnets kept out of reach. Inclusion: every mode of communication earns a block, pass is always OK, class totals only, blocks never taken away, no individual ranking. Rule 7 and logo rules: original names, characters and page designs; final logo kit from brand/logo/ (horizontal lockup, one-colour white on the story's tomato and sky covers); blocks appear only as game art and illustration, never as a logo, product mark or series mark, and the Talk Tower title is set in type. Privacy: the bonus asks for an email only (no child names); the kit asks families and teachers not to post children's names or faces. Legal: copyright line '© 2026 AlphaPlay LLC. Play Before Pixels is a trade name of AlphaPlay LLC.' on the license page, the story copyright page and in every page footer with the short license notice (per legal/protection/digital-product-license.md, Part A). The license page is drafted from the DRAFT license template and needs attorney review. PDF metadata carries the copyright and license URL. Printing: printables are Letter and A4 with 0.5 in margins and no bleed; test-print at 100% before sale. faq.q: Can I buy it as a gift for a teacher?
faq.a: Yes. Buy the license the teacher needs and forward the download email; the license belongs to the teacher or site named in it. [VERIFY that the store platform can send the download straight to a gift recipient.]

faq.q: Can our PTA or parent group buy it for the school?
faq.a: Yes. A PTA or parent group may buy the site license for its school, and the certificate names the school. Using the kit at a PTA family event is a question for the license page [counsel to confirm].

faq.q: Can a library use it at storytime?
faq.a: Yes, with a site license naming your library: play and read aloud in person, and copy the family pages for the families you serve. Online storytime only in a private, registration-only session, with no public recordings [counsel to confirm].

faq.q: Does it work for children who sign, point or use a talking device?
faq.a: Yes. Words in any language, signing, pointing, picture cards and a tap on a talking device all earn a block, and 'pass' is always OK. The kit counts a talking device as a child's voice, not screen time.
Not yet. Children can take their turns in any language, and the family page says to talk, sing and read in the language you know best. Spanish family pages are planned, made by a human translator.
Ages 3–7 (preschool to grade 2). Each variation lists a starting age in months. For ages 3–4, start with two blocks (comment and listen) and short rounds.
Digital downloads follow the shop's published refund policy [link the policy page at launch].

faq.q: Is it on Amazon or other stores?
faq.a: No Amazon edition: a licensed classroom kit can't be sold as a paperback. A Teachers Pay Teachers and Etsy edition may follow.
